fundamentals.name: Netflix, Inc.
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Netflix, Inc. provides entertainment services worldwide. The company offers television (TV) series, documentaries, feature films, games, and live programming across various genres and languages. It also provides members the ability to receive streaming content through a host of internet-connected devices, including TVs, digital video players, TV set-top boxes, and mobile devices. Netflix, Inc. was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Los Gatos, California.

judgment.summary: Netflix exhibits strong growth and profitability metrics, supported by a solid balance sheet and high analyst conviction, though its valuation is on the higher side.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter missed EPS estimates by 1.4%; next earnings date is 2026-07-16.
positives: Revenue growth 16.2% YoY and earnings growth 86.4% YoY indicate robust top and bottom-line expansion.
Operating margin of 32.3% and profit margin of 28.5% demonstrate excellent profitability.
Return on equity at 48.5% and return on assets at 15.4% show efficient use of capital.
Free cash flow of $25.99B TTM provides significant financial flexibility.
Analyst consensus is 'buy' with a mean target of $114.15, suggesting upside potential.
negatives: Trailing P/E of 25.70 and Forward P/E of 20.74 suggest a premium valuation.
PEG ratio of 1.61 indicates that growth may not fully justify the current stock price.
Debt/Equity ratio of 53.79%, while manageable with strong cash flow, warrants monitoring.
Last quarter's EPS missed estimates by 1.4%.

news.paragraph: Netflix is facing headwinds, with recent reports highlighting factors dragging down its stock price, even as some analysts view it as a high-quality compounder on sale. The company has appointed a new Chairman, Jay Hoag, who will focus on advertising and live events, signaling a strategic shift. Despite these challenges, Netflix is expected to maintain its global lead in the streaming market amidst industry consolidation.
